meta.name: The Shape of Intelligence — AI history dataset

events.title: A logical calculus of nervous activity
events.summary: McCulloch and Pitts show that a simplified neuron is a logic gate, and that networks of them can compute anything a Turing machine can.
orgs: University of Illinois College of Medicine

sources.title: A logical calculus of the ideas immanent in nervous activity (Bulletin of Mathematical Biophysics)
Full text of the 1943 paper (CMU copy)

events.title: The stored-program computer
events.summary: Von Neumann's First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC lays out the stored-program architecture, and describes its logic in McCulloch–Pitts neurons.

sources.title: First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC (1945)
First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC, annotated reprint (IEEE Annals of the History of Computing)

events.title: A mathematical theory of communication
events.summary: Shannon defines information as a measurable quantity, the bit, and gives the entropy and channel-capacity results that every model of language still rests on.

sources.title: A Mathematical Theory of Communication (Bell System Technical Journal)
Reprint of the 1948 paper (Harvard mirror)

events.title: Cells that fire together wire together
events.summary: Donald Hebb proposes that learning happens by strengthening the connection between neurons that are active at the same time, the first learning rule for a network.

sources.title: The Organization of Behavior: A Neuropsychological Theory (Wiley, 1949), full text
The Organization of Behavior (2002 reissue)

events.title: Programming a computer for playing chess
events.summary: Shannon sets out minimax search with an evaluation function and estimates the game tree at 10¹²⁰ positions, the plan Deep Blue followed 47 years later.

sources.title: Programming a Computer for Playing Chess (Philosophical Magazine, 1950)
Text of the paper (mirror)

events.title: Computing machinery and intelligence
events.summary: Turing replaces the question 'can machines think?' with a test, predicts learning machines, and answers the objections that are still being raised today.

sources.title: Computing Machinery and Intelligence (Mind, vol. LIX, no. 236)
Computing Machinery and Intelligence at Oxford Academic

events.title: SNARC, the first neural network machine
events.summary: Minsky and Edmonds build a 40-neuron learning machine from vacuum tubes and surplus bomber parts, wired to reinforce whatever it did last.

sources.title: Jeremy Bernstein, 'A.I.', The New Yorker, 14 December 1981 (profile of Minsky describing SNARC)
Stochastic neural analog reinforcement calculator (summary and references)

events.title: The Dartmouth workshop names the field
events.summary: A two-month summer meeting at Dartmouth College, proposed under the new phrase 'artificial intelligence', gathers the people who will run the field for thirty years.

sources.title: A Proposal for the Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence (31 August 1955)
A Proposal for the Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence (AI Magazine reprint, 2006)
Artificial Intelligence (AI) Coined at Dartmouth (Dartmouth College)

events.title: Logic Theorist proves its first theorems
events.summary: Newell, Shaw and Simon's program proves 38 theorems from Principia Mathematica by heuristic search, the first working artificial intelligence program.

sources.title: The logic theory machine: a complex information processing system (IRE Transactions on Information Theory, 1956)
The Logic Theory Machine (RAND paper P-868)

events.title: Lisp
events.summary: McCarthy designs Lisp, a language built on recursion and symbolic lists, which becomes the native tongue of AI research for thirty years.

sources.title: Recursive Functions of Symbolic Expressions and Their Computation by Machine, Part I (Communications of the ACM, 1960)
History of Lisp (McCarthy, 1979)

events.title: The perceptron learns
events.summary: Rosenblatt's perceptron adjusts its own weights from examples; the US Navy demonstrates it and the press announces an 'embryo' that will walk, talk and reproduce.

sources.title: The perceptron: a probabilistic model for information storage and organization in the brain (Psychological Review, 1958)
New Navy Device Learns By Doing (The New York Times, 8 July 1958)

events.title: Samuel's checkers program coins 'machine learning'
events.summary: Arthur Samuel's checkers player improves by playing itself and tuning its evaluation function, and his paper gives the field its name.

sources.title: Some Studies in Machine Learning Using the Game of Checkers (IBM Journal of Research and Development, 1959)
IBM history: early computer games and Samuel's checkers

events.title: ADALINE and the least-mean-squares rule
events.summary: Widrow and Hoff's adaptive neuron learns by gradient descent on squared error, the delta rule that backpropagation later generalises.

sources.title: Adaptive Switching Circuits (IRE WESCON Convention Record, 1960)
30 years of adaptive neural networks: perceptron, Madaline, and backpropagation (Proceedings of the IEEE, 1990)

events.title: Unimate, the first industrial robot
events.summary: George Devol's programmable arm starts work on a General Motors line, lifting hot die-castings; robotics and AI begin as separate fields.

sources.title: Unimate (Encyclopaedia Britannica)
George Devol, National Inventors Hall of Fame

events.title: ARPA funds Project MAC
events.summary: The US Advanced Research Projects Agency gives MIT $2.2 million for computing and AI research, beginning two decades of near-unconditional military funding.

sources.title: MIT CSAIL: mission and history
Project MAC (Multicians history)

events.title: DENDRAL, the first expert system
events.summary: Feigenbaum, Lederberg and Djerassi start a program that infers molecular structure from mass-spectrometry data using rules elicited from chemists.

sources.title: DENDRAL: a case study of the first expert system for scientific hypothesis formation (Artificial Intelligence, 1993)
The Dendral Project (Joshua Lederberg papers, US National Library of Medicine)

events.title: Moore's law
events.summary: Gordon Moore observes that the number of components on a chip doubles every year, an exponential that would deliver the compute behind every later breakthrough.

sources.title: Cramming more components onto integrated circuits (Electronics, 19 April 1965)
Cramming more components onto integrated circuits (Proceedings of the IEEE reprint, 1998)

events.title: ELIZA
events.summary: Weizenbaum's ELIZA turns a person's sentences back as a Rogerian therapist would; people confide in it, and its author spends the rest of his life alarmed.

sources.title: ELIZA: a computer program for the study of natural language communication between man and machine (Communications of the ACM, 1966)
ELIZA paper, full text (Stanford CS124 copy)

events.title: Shakey, the first mobile robot that reasons
events.summary: SRI's Shakey plans its own routes with a camera, a logic-based planner and the A* search algorithm, which its team invents for the job.

sources.title: Shakey the Robot (SRI International)
A Formal Basis for the Heuristic Determination of Minimum Cost Paths (IEEE Transactions on Systems Science and Cybernetics, 1968)

events.title: The ALPAC report ends machine translation funding
events.summary: A US government committee concludes machine translation is slower, worse and more expensive than human translation; funding stops for twenty years.

sources.title: Language and Machines: Computers in Translation and Linguistics (National Academies Press, 1966)
ALPAC (background and consequences)

events.title: Nearest neighbour classification
events.summary: Cover and Hart prove that classifying a point by its nearest labelled neighbour has at most twice the error of the best possible classifier.

sources.title: Nearest neighbor pattern classification (IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, 1967)

events.title: HAL 9000
events.summary: 2001: A Space Odyssey gives the public a calm, competent, murderous computer; HAL fixes the popular image of machine intelligence for fifty years.

sources.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey (AFI Catalog of Feature Films)
2001: A Space Odyssey (1968)

events.title: Perceptrons
events.summary: Minsky and Papert prove that a single-layer perceptron cannot learn XOR or connectedness; the book is read as a verdict on neural networks and the money leaves.

sources.title: Perceptrons: An Introduction to Computational Geometry (MIT Press, 1969)
A sociological study of the official history of the perceptrons controversy (Social Studies of Science, 1996)

events.title: Reverse-mode automatic differentiation
events.summary: Seppo Linnainmaa's master's thesis gives the algorithm for computing all the derivatives of a nested function in one backward sweep, the mathematics of backpropagation.

sources.title: Taylor expansion of the accumulated rounding error (BIT Numerical Mathematics, 1976)
Who invented the reverse mode of differentiation? (Griewank, Documenta Mathematica, 2012)

events.title: SHRDLU understands a world of blocks
events.summary: Terry Winograd's program holds a real conversation about a simulated table of blocks, resolving pronouns and reasons; it is the high-water mark of hand-built language understanding.

sources.title: Procedures as a Representation for Data in a Computer Program for Understanding Natural Language (MIT, 1971)
SHRDLU (Terry Winograd's project page, Stanford)

events.title: Prolog
events.summary: Colmerauer and Roussel create a language in which a program is a set of logical facts and rules, and running it is proving a theorem.

sources.title: The birth of Prolog (ACM SIGPLAN History of Programming Languages II, 1993)

events.title: The Lighthill report
events.summary: Sir James Lighthill's review for the UK Science Research Council finds AI has failed to deliver on its promises; British funding collapses and the first winter begins.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence: A General Survey (Lighthill, 1973), full text

events.title: MYCIN diagnoses infections
events.summary: Shortliffe's MYCIN uses about 600 if-then rules with certainty factors to recommend antibiotics, matching specialists in blind evaluation but never used on a patient.

sources.title: A model of inexact reasoning in medicine (Mathematical Biosciences, 1975)

events.title: Werbos applies backpropagation to neural networks
events.summary: Paul Werbos's Harvard thesis 'Beyond Regression' describes training multi-layer networks by propagating errors backwards; almost nobody reads it for a decade.

sources.title: The Roots of Backpropagation: From Ordered Derivatives to Neural Networks and Political Forecasting (Wiley, 1994), which reprints the 1974 thesis

events.title: Genetic algorithms
events.summary: John Holland's Adaptation in Natural and Artificial Systems formalises search by mutation, crossover and selection, an alternative to gradients that outlasts the winter.

sources.title: Adaptation in Natural and Artificial Systems (MIT Press edition)

events.title: AAAI is founded
events.summary: American AI researchers form their own society during the winter; its first conference, at Stanford in August 1980, draws a thousand people.
orgs: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence

sources.title: About AAAI

events.title: The Stanford Cart crosses a room
events.summary: Hans Moravec's camera-guided cart navigates a chair-filled room on its own in about five hours, the first autonomous vehicle to steer by vision.

sources.title: Obstacle Avoidance and Navigation in the Real World by a Seeing Robot Rover (Moravec, Stanford PhD thesis, 1980)

events.title: XCON goes into production at DEC
events.summary: McDermott's R1, renamed XCON, configures VAX computer orders from rules and saves Digital Equipment an estimated $25 million a year; the expert-systems boom begins.

sources.title: R1: A rule-based configurer of computer systems (Artificial Intelligence, 1982)

events.title: The Neocognitron
events.summary: Fukushima's layered network of local feature detectors and pooling recognises patterns regardless of position, the architecture of the convolutional network.
orgs: NHK Science and Technology Research Laboratories

sources.title: Neocognitron: a self-organizing neural network model for a mechanism of pattern recognition unaffected by shift in position (Biological Cybernetics, 1980)

events.title: Symbolics and the Lisp machine business
events.summary: MIT's Lisp machine spins out into Symbolics and Lisp Machines Inc., creating a hardware industry for AI whose collapse will mark the second winter.

sources.title: The Lisp Machine (MIT AI Memo 444, 1977)

events.title: Self-organising maps
events.summary: Teuvo Kohonen's network arranges its neurons so that similar inputs land on nearby units, learning a map of the data with no labels at all.

sources.title: Self-organized formation of topologically correct feature maps (Biological Cybernetics, 1982)

events.title: Japan launches the Fifth Generation project
events.summary: Japan's MITI funds a ten-year national programme to build parallel machines that reason in logic; the West panics into funding of its own.
orgs: Ministry of International Trade and Industry
Institute for New Generation Computer Technology

sources.title: The fifth generation project, a trip report (Communications of the ACM, 1983)

events.title: The Hopfield network
events.summary: John Hopfield shows that a symmetric network of binary neurons has an energy function, and that memories can be stored as the minima it settles into.

sources.title: Neural networks and physical systems with emergent collective computational abilities (PNAS, 1982)
Scientific background to the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics (Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences)

events.title: DARPA's Strategic Computing Initiative
events.summary: The US answers Japan with a billion-dollar programme for machine intelligence in weapons, funding a decade of expert systems, vision and autonomous vehicles.

sources.title: Strategic Computing: DARPA and the Quest for Machine Intelligence, 1983–1993 (MIT Press, 2002)

events.title: Cyc sets out to write down common sense
events.summary: Douglas Lenat begins a project to encode everything a person knows as logical assertions; forty years and millions of rules later it is still going.

sources.title: CYC: Using Common Sense Knowledge to Overcome Brittleness and Knowledge Acquisition Bottlenecks (AI Magazine, 1986)

events.title: 'AI winter' is named
events.summary: At the AAAI conference, Minsky and Schank warn that hype has outrun results and that a collapse in funding, an 'AI winter', is coming. It does.
orgs: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence

sources.title: The Dark Ages of AI: A Panel Discussion at AAAI-84 (AI Magazine, 1985)

events.title: The Terminator
events.summary: James Cameron's film gives the world Skynet, a defence network that becomes self-aware and launches a war on humanity; the image never leaves the debate.

sources.title: The Terminator (1984)

events.title: The Boltzmann machine
events.summary: Ackley, Hinton and Sejnowski add noise and hidden units to the Hopfield network and derive a learning rule, the first for a network with hidden layers.

sources.title: A learning algorithm for Boltzmann machines (Cognitive Science, 1985)
Scientific background to the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics

events.title: The Connection Machine
events.summary: Danny Hillis's 65,536-processor computer is designed to run brain-like computations in parallel; it finds its market in physics and databases instead.

sources.title: The Connection Machine (MIT Press, 1985)

events.title: ID3 and decision-tree learning
events.summary: Ross Quinlan's algorithm grows a tree of yes/no questions from data by choosing the split with the most information gain; it becomes industry's workhorse.

sources.title: Induction of decision trees (Machine Learning, 1986)

events.title: Backpropagation
events.summary: Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams show that multi-layer networks can learn internal representations by propagating errors backwards; Perceptrons is answered.

sources.title: Learning representations by back-propagating errors (Nature, 9 October 1986)
Learning representations by back-propagating errors (Nature article page)
Scientific background to the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics

events.title: The Lisp machine market collapses
events.summary: Specialised AI hardware worth half a billion dollars a year loses to cheaper workstations; expert-systems firms follow, and the second winter begins.

sources.title: AI: The Tumultuous History of the Search for Artificial Intelligence (Crevier, 1993), full text

events.title: NETtalk learns to read aloud
events.summary: Sejnowski and Rosenberg's backpropagation network learns to pronounce English text; a recording of it babbling and then speaking makes the case in public.

sources.title: Parallel networks that learn to pronounce English text (Complex Systems, 1987)

events.title: The first NIPS conference
events.summary: Neural Information Processing Systems meets in Denver, bringing physicists, neuroscientists and computer scientists into one room; it becomes the field's main stage.

sources.title: Proceedings of the first NIPS conference, Denver, 1987

events.title: Bayesian networks
events.summary: Judea Pearl's book makes probability the language of uncertain reasoning, replacing the ad hoc certainty factors of expert systems with graphs of causes.

sources.title: Probabilistic Reasoning in Intelligent Systems: Networks of Plausible Inference (Morgan Kaufmann, 1988)
Judea Pearl, ACM A.M. Turing Award 2011

events.title: Temporal-difference learning
events.summary: Richard Sutton formalises learning from the difference between successive predictions, the method inside Samuel's checkers player, TD-Gammon and AlphaGo.

sources.title: Learning to predict by the methods of temporal differences (Machine Learning, 1988)

events.title: ALVINN drives a van with a neural network
events.summary: Dean Pomerleau's three-layer network steers Carnegie Mellon's Navlab from camera images, trained on a human driver; the first learned self-driving system.

sources.title: ALVINN: An Autonomous Land Vehicle in a Neural Network (Carnegie Mellon, 1989)

events.title: Q-learning
events.summary: Chris Watkins's thesis gives an algorithm that learns the value of every action in every state from experience alone, with a proof that it converges to the best policy.

sources.title: Learning from Delayed Rewards (Watkins, PhD thesis, University of Cambridge, 1989)
Q-learning (Watkins and Dayan, Machine Learning, 1992)

events.title: The universal approximation theorem
events.summary: Cybenko, and separately Hornik, Stinchcombe and White, prove that one hidden layer of sigmoid units can approximate any continuous function; the question becomes learning, not capacity.

sources.title: Approximation by superpositions of a sigmoidal function (Mathematics of Control, Signals and Systems, 1989)
Multilayer feedforward networks are universal approximators (Neural Networks, 1989)

events.title: LeNet reads handwritten postcodes
events.summary: Yann LeCun trains a convolutional network by backpropagation on US Postal Service digits; the first deep network in real use, and the ancestor of AlexNet.

sources.title: Backpropagation applied to handwritten zip code recognition (Neural Computation, 1989)

events.title: Finding structure in time
events.summary: Jeffrey Elman's recurrent network feeds its own hidden state back as input and learns grammar-like structure from sequences of words with no labels.

sources.title: Finding structure in time (Cognitive Science, 1990)

events.title: Boosting: weak learners made strong
events.summary: Robert Schapire proves that any learner slightly better than chance can be combined into one as accurate as you like; ensembles become a science.

sources.title: The strength of weak learnability (Machine Learning, 1990)

events.title: The vanishing gradient problem
events.summary: Sepp Hochreiter's diploma thesis shows why deep and recurrent networks fail to learn: error signals shrink exponentially as they travel back through layers.

sources.title: Untersuchungen zu dynamischen neuronalen Netzen (Hochreiter, diploma thesis, TU München, 1991)

events.title: The first Loebner Prize
events.summary: The Turing test becomes an annual contest in Boston; the winning program fools judges by making typing errors, and the test's weaknesses become a spectacle.

sources.title: Loebner Prize (history and results)

events.title: TD-Gammon reaches world-class backgammon
events.summary: Gerald Tesauro's network learns backgammon by playing itself with temporal-difference learning and reaches the level of the best humans, changing how they play.

sources.title: Practical issues in temporal difference learning (Machine Learning, 1992)
Temporal difference learning and TD-Gammon (Communications of the ACM, 1995)

events.title: The Fifth Generation project ends
events.summary: Japan's ten-year programme closes with good parallel machines and none of the reasoning computers it promised; the last large bet on symbolic AI is written off.
orgs: Institute for New Generation Computer Technology
Ministry of International Trade and Industry

sources.title: 'Fifth Generation' Became Japan's Lost Generation (The New York Times, 5 June 1992)

events.title: Chinook becomes checkers champion
events.summary: Jonathan Schaeffer's program takes the world checkers title when Marion Tinsley, the greatest human player, withdraws ill; the first world title held by a machine.

sources.title: CHINOOK: The World Man-Machine Checkers Champion (AI Magazine, 1996)

events.title: Support-vector machines
events.summary: Cortes and Vapnik's classifier finds the widest margin between classes and, with the kernel trick, does it in spaces of any dimension; it rules the field for a decade.

sources.title: Support-vector networks (Machine Learning, 1995)

events.title: Deep Blue beats Kasparov
events.summary: IBM's chess machine wins a six-game match against the world champion, 3.5 to 2.5; chess falls to search, and the public takes it as a verdict on thinking.

sources.title: Deep Blue (IBM history)
Deep Blue (Artificial Intelligence, 2002)

events.title: Long short-term memory
events.summary: Hochreiter and Schmidhuber's memory cell with gates lets recurrent networks learn across a thousand steps; it becomes the engine of speech, translation and text until 2017.

sources.title: Long Short-Term Memory (Neural Computation, 1997)
Long Short-Term Memory (MIT Press Direct)

events.title: PageRank and the anatomy of Google
events.summary: Brin and Page rank web pages by the links between them, an eigenvector of the web; search becomes the first application of statistics to the whole internet.

sources.title: The anatomy of a large-scale hypertextual Web search engine (Computer Networks, 1998)
The Anatomy of a Large-Scale Hypertextual Web Search Engine (Stanford InfoLab)

events.title: MNIST and LeNet-5
events.summary: LeCun, Bottou, Bengio and Haffner's paper fixes the convolutional network design and releases the 70,000-digit dataset that becomes the field's first shared yardstick.

sources.title: Gradient-based learning applied to document recognition (Proceedings of the IEEE, 1998)
The MNIST database of handwritten digits

events.title: The first GPU
events.summary: NVIDIA's GeForce 256 puts geometry transformation and lighting on a single chip and calls it a graphics processing unit; the hardware of deep learning arrives for games.

sources.title: NVIDIA corporate timeline

events.title: ASIMO walks
events.summary: Honda unveils a 1.2-metre humanoid that walks, climbs stairs and shakes hands; the public image of the robot updates, and the intelligence inside stays scripted.

sources.title: ASIMO (history and specifications)

events.title: Wikipedia launches
events.summary: A free encyclopaedia anyone can edit goes live; two decades later its text is in the training data of every language model and is the largest single curated corpus on Earth.

sources.title: Wikimedia Foundation: about
History of Wikipedia

events.title: Random forests
events.summary: Leo Breiman averages hundreds of decision trees, each grown on a random sample of data and features, and gets a method that is accurate, robust and hard to overfit.

sources.title: Random Forests (Machine Learning, 2001)

events.title: Roomba
events.summary: iRobot sells a vacuum cleaner that navigates by bumping into things; the first robot to live in millions of homes runs almost no AI at all.

sources.title: Roomba (product history)

events.title: A neural probabilistic language model
events.summary: Bengio's group learns a vector for every word and predicts the next word from the vectors of the last few; word embeddings and neural language models begin here.

sources.title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model (Journal of Machine Learning Research, 2003)

events.title: MapReduce
events.summary: Google describes how it processes the whole web on thousands of cheap machines with two functions; the infrastructure for training on internet-scale data becomes ordinary.

sources.title: MapReduce: Simplified Data Processing on Large Clusters (OSDI, 2004)
MapReduce: simplified data processing on large clusters (Communications of the ACM, 2008)

events.title: Stanley wins the DARPA Grand Challenge
events.summary: Stanford's autonomous Volkswagen drives 212 kilometres of Nevada desert in under seven hours, a year after no vehicle managed twelve; machine learning steers the winner.

sources.title: Stanley: The robot that won the DARPA Grand Challenge (Journal of Field Robotics, 2006)

events.title: Deep belief networks and the word 'deep'
events.summary: Hinton, Osindero and Teh train a deep network one layer at a time as stacked Boltzmann machines and then fine-tune it; deep learning gets its name and its first results.

sources.title: A fast learning algorithm for deep belief nets (Neural Computation, 2006)
Reducing the dimensionality of data with neural networks (Science, 2006)

events.title: The Netflix Prize
events.summary: Netflix releases 100 million ratings and offers a million dollars for a 10% better recommender; three years of open competition teach the field ensembles and matrix factorisation.

sources.title: Lessons from the Netflix prize challenge (ACM SIGKDD Explorations, 2007)
Netflix Prize (competition history and results)

events.title: CUDA
events.summary: NVIDIA releases a programming model that lets ordinary C code run on the thousands of cores of a graphics card; GPUs become general-purpose, and deep learning gets its engine.

sources.title: Scalable parallel programming with CUDA (ACM Queue, 2008)
CUDA Toolkit (NVIDIA Developer)

events.title: Checkers is solved
events.summary: After eighteen years of computation, Schaeffer's team proves that perfect play in checkers is a draw; the first major game to be solved outright.

sources.title: Checkers Is Solved (Science, 2007)

events.title: Deep learning moves to GPUs
events.summary: Raina, Madhavan and Ng train deep belief networks on graphics cards seventy times faster than on CPUs; the hardware and the method find each other.

sources.title: Large-scale deep unsupervised learning using graphics processors (ICML, 2009)

events.title: ImageNet
events.summary: Fei-Fei Li's team releases 3.2 million labelled images across thousands of categories, and the annual challenge on it becomes the arena where deep learning wins.

sources.title: ImageNet: A large-scale hierarchical image database (CVPR, 2009)
ImageNet
ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge (International Journal of Computer Vision, 2015)

events.title: Rectified linear units
events.summary: Nair and Hinton replace the sigmoid with max(0, x); the gradient no longer vanishes through active units and deep networks train several times faster.

sources.title: Rectified Linear Units Improve Restricted Boltzmann Machines (ICML, 2010)
Deep Sparse Rectifier Neural Networks (AISTATS, 2011)

events.title: DeepMind is founded
events.summary: Demis Hassabis, Shane Legg and Mustafa Suleyman start a London company to 'solve intelligence' with reinforcement learning and neuroscience; it produces AlphaGo and AlphaFold.

sources.title: About Google DeepMind

events.title: Watson wins Jeopardy!
events.summary: IBM's question-answering system beats the two best human players of the quiz show over three broadcast nights; language, not chess, becomes the public test.

sources.title: Building Watson: An Overview of the DeepQA Project (AI Magazine, 2010)
Watson, Jeopardy! champion (IBM history)

events.title: Siri ships on the iPhone
events.summary: Apple puts a voice assistant on the iPhone 4S, descended from DARPA's CALO project at SRI; talking to a computer becomes something hundreds of millions of people do.

sources.title: Apple Launches iPhone 4S, iOS 5 and iCloud (Apple Newsroom, 4 October 2011)
Siri (SRI International)

events.title: Google Brain's network discovers cats
events.summary: A billion-parameter network trained on ten million YouTube frames across 16,000 cores learns, unsupervised, a neuron that fires for cat faces; scale enters the vocabulary.

sources.title: Building high-level features using large scale unsupervised learning (ICML, 2012; arXiv:1112.6209)

events.title: Dropout
events.summary: Hinton's group randomly switches off half the units during each training step, so no unit can rely on another; overfitting drops sharply and AlexNet adopts it.

sources.title: Improving neural networks by preventing co-adaptation of feature detectors (arXiv:1207.0580)
Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting (Journal of Machine Learning Research, 2014)

events.title: AlexNet wins ImageNet
events.summary: Krizhevsky, Sutskever and Hinton's convolutional network, trained on two gaming GPUs, cuts the ImageNet error rate from 26% to 15%; the deep-learning era begins.

sources.title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (NeurIPS, 2012)
ImageNet classification with deep convolutional neural networks (Communications of the ACM, 2017)
ILSVRC 2012 results

events.title: Word2vec
events.summary: Mikolov's team at Google learns word vectors from billions of words in hours, and shows that king − man + woman ≈ queen; meaning becomes arithmetic.

sources.title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space (arXiv:1301.3781)
Distributed Representations of Words and Phrases and their Compositionality (NeurIPS, 2013)

events.title: Deep Q-networks play Atari
events.summary: DeepMind's network learns to play Atari games from raw pixels and the score alone, using Watkins's Q-learning with a convolutional network as the value table.

sources.title: Playing Atari with Deep Reinforcement Learning (arXiv:1312.5602)
Human-level control through deep reinforcement learning (Nature, 2015)

events.title: Google buys DeepMind
events.summary: Google pays around £400 million for a three-year-old London research company with no products; frontier AI research becomes a thing the largest companies own.

sources.title: Google acquires UK artificial intelligence startup DeepMind (The Guardian, 27 January 2014)

events.title: Generative adversarial networks
events.summary: Goodfellow trains two networks against each other, a forger and a detective, and gets a generator that learns to produce realistic images with no likelihood at all.

sources.title: Generative Adversarial Networks (arXiv:1406.2661)
Generative Adversarial Nets (NeurIPS, 2014)
Generative adversarial networks (Communications of the ACM, 2020)

events.title: Superintelligence
events.summary: Nick Bostrom's book argues that a machine smarter than its makers could be the last invention they need to make, and possibly the last they do; Musk and Gates recommend it.

sources.title: Superintelligence: Paths, Dangers, Strategies (Oxford University Press)

events.title: Attention
events.summary: Bahdanau, Cho and Bengio let a translation model look back at every source word and learn which to weigh; the mechanism at the heart of the transformer appears.

sources.title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate (arXiv:1409.0473)
Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate (ICLR, 2015)

events.title: Sequence to sequence learning
events.summary: Sutskever, Vinyals and Le show that a large LSTM can translate English to French end to end, with no linguistic pipeline; text-in, text-out becomes the shape of the field.

sources.title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks (arXiv:1409.3215)
Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks (NeurIPS, 2014)

events.title: Adam
events.summary: Kingma and Ba's optimiser adapts the learning rate for every parameter from running averages of the gradient and its square; it becomes the default way to train almost everything.

sources.title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization (arXiv:1412.6980)

events.title: Batch normalisation
events.summary: Ioffe and Szegedy normalise the activations inside a network during training; deep networks train in a fraction of the steps and much deeper stacks become practical.

sources.title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift (arXiv:1502.03167)

events.title: Diffusion models
events.summary: Sohl-Dickstein and colleagues destroy data by adding noise step by step and train a network to reverse the process; the idea waits five years to become the way images are made.

sources.title: Deep Unsupervised Learning using Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics (arXiv:1503.03585)

events.title: TensorFlow is open-sourced
events.summary: Google releases the framework that runs its own deep learning; the tools of the frontier become free, and PyTorch's arrival a year later sets the standard everyone uses.

sources.title: TensorFlow: Large-Scale Machine Learning on Heterogeneous Distributed Systems (arXiv:1603.04467)
TensorFlow: Google's latest machine learning system, open sourced for everyone (Google Research blog, 2015)

events.title: Residual networks
events.summary: He, Zhang, Ren and Sun add skip connections so each layer learns a correction to its input; 152-layer networks train easily and beat humans on ImageNet.

sources.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition (arXiv:1512.03385)
Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition (CVPR, 2016)

events.title: OpenAI is founded
events.summary: Musk, Altman, Brockman and Sutskever announce a non-profit laboratory with a billion dollars pledged, to build AI 'for the benefit of humanity' outside Google's control.

sources.title: Introducing OpenAI (11 December 2015)

events.title: AlphaGo beats Lee Sedol
events.summary: DeepMind's program wins four games to one against one of the greatest Go players, a decade before it was thought possible; move 37 shows a machine playing beautifully.

sources.title: Mastering the game of Go with deep neural networks and tree search (Nature, 2016)
Google AI algorithm masters ancient game of Go (Nature news, 2016)

events.title: Tay
events.summary: Microsoft's teenage chatbot learns from Twitter and is taken offline within sixteen hours after users teach it to produce racist and abusive posts.

sources.title: Learning from Tay's introduction (Microsoft, 25 March 2016)

events.title: Google reveals the TPU
events.summary: Google discloses that a custom chip for neural-network inference has been running in its data centres for a year; the hardware race for AI moves beyond GPUs.

sources.title: Google supercharges machine learning tasks with TPU custom chip (Google Cloud blog, 2016)
In-Datacenter Performance Analysis of a Tensor Processing Unit (arXiv:1704.04760)

events.title: WaveNet
events.summary: DeepMind generates raw audio one sample at a time with a dilated convolutional network; synthetic speech stops sounding synthetic.

sources.title: WaveNet: A Generative Model for Raw Audio (arXiv:1609.03499)

events.title: Google Translate goes neural
events.summary: Google replaces its phrase-based translation system with a deep LSTM with attention, for hundreds of millions of users; error rates fall by more than half on some languages.

sources.title: Google's Neural Machine Translation System: Bridging the Gap between Human and Machine Translation (arXiv:1609.08144)
A Neural Network for Machine Translation, at Production Scale (Google Research blog, 2016)

events.title: The Asilomar AI Principles
events.summary: Researchers and executives meeting at Asilomar agree 23 principles for beneficial AI, signed by thousands; the safety conversation gets a founding document.

sources.title: Asilomar AI Principles (Future of Life Institute, 2017)

events.title: Attention is all you need
events.summary: Eight Google researchers drop recurrence entirely and build a sequence model from attention alone; the transformer trains in parallel, scales without limit, and becomes the architecture of everything.

sources.title: Attention Is All You Need (arXiv:1706.03762)
Attention Is All You Need (NeurIPS, 2017)
Transformer: A Novel Neural Network Architecture for Language Understanding (Google Research blog, 2017)

events.title: Deep reinforcement learning from human preferences
events.summary: Christiano and colleagues train agents from a human's choices between pairs of video clips instead of a coded reward; the method that will align chatbots is born.

sources.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences (arXiv:1706.03741)

events.title: AlphaGo Zero learns from nothing
events.summary: A new version starts from random play with no human games at all, and after three days beats the AlphaGo that beat Lee Sedol 100 games to 0.

sources.title: Mastering the game of Go without human knowledge (Nature, 2017)

events.title: GPT: generative pre-training
events.summary: OpenAI pre-trains a twelve-layer transformer decoder to predict the next word in 7,000 books, then fine-tunes it; one model tops nine language benchmarks.

sources.title: Improving Language Understanding with Unsupervised Learning (OpenAI, 11 June 2018)
Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training (paper)

events.title: BERT
events.summary: Google's bidirectional transformer, pre-trained to fill in masked words, sets new records on eleven language tasks and goes into Google Search within a year.

sources.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding (arXiv:1810.04805)
BERT (NAACL, 2019)

events.title: AlphaFold enters the protein-folding contest
events.summary: DeepMind's first AlphaFold wins the CASP13 structure-prediction competition by a wide margin, using deep networks to predict distances between amino acids.

sources.title: Improved protein structure prediction using potentials from deep learning (Nature, 2020)

events.title: GPT-2 and the model too dangerous to release
events.summary: OpenAI's 1.5-billion-parameter model writes coherent pages of text from a prompt; the lab withholds the full weights over misuse fears, and the argument about openness begins.

sources.title: Better language models and their implications (OpenAI, 14 February 2019)
Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners (paper)

events.title: The bitter lesson
events.summary: Richard Sutton's short essay argues that seventy years of AI show one thing: methods that use more computation beat methods that use more human knowledge, every time.

sources.title: The Bitter Lesson (Sutton, 13 March 2019)

events.title: The Turing Award goes to deep learning
events.summary: Bengio, Hinton and LeCun receive computing's highest honour for the work that two winters had dismissed; the establishment concedes.

sources.title: 2018 ACM A.M. Turing Award: Bengio, Hinton, LeCun

events.title: Scaling laws for neural language models
events.summary: Kaplan and colleagues at OpenAI find that language-model loss falls as a smooth power law in parameters, data and compute across seven orders of magnitude; size becomes a plan.

sources.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models (arXiv:2001.08361)
Deep Learning Scaling is Predictable, Empirically (arXiv:1712.00409)

events.title: GPT-3
events.summary: A 175-billion-parameter model learns new tasks from a few examples in its prompt, with no fine-tuning; the era of prompting, and of models as a product, begins.

sources.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners (arXiv:2005.14165)
Language Models are Few-Shot Learners (NeurIPS, 2020)

events.title: Denoising diffusion probabilistic models
events.summary: Ho, Jain and Abbeel simplify the 2015 diffusion recipe into predicting the noise, and match adversarial networks on image quality; the generative field changes course.

sources.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (arXiv:2006.11239)

events.title: Learning to summarise from human feedback
events.summary: OpenAI applies preference learning to GPT-style models: people pick the better of two summaries, a reward model learns the picks, and the language model is optimised against it.

sources.title: Learning to summarize from human feedback (arXiv:2009.01325)

events.title: An image is worth 16×16 words
events.summary: Google cuts images into patches, feeds them to a standard transformer with no convolutions, and matches the best vision models given enough data; one architecture for everything.

sources.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale (arXiv:2010.11929)

events.title: AlphaFold 2 solves protein structure prediction
events.summary: At CASP14 DeepMind's rebuilt system predicts protein shapes to experimental accuracy; a fifty-year problem is judged solved and 200 million structures follow.

sources.title: Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold (Nature, 2021)
'It will change everything': DeepMind's AI makes gigantic leap in solving protein structures (Nature news, 2020)

events.title: CLIP and DALL·E
events.summary: OpenAI releases a model that matches images to captions across 400 million pairs, and a model that draws images from text; pictures become something you ask for.

sources.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision (arXiv:2103.00020)
Zero-Shot Text-to-Image Generation (arXiv:2102.12092)
CLIP: Connecting text and images (OpenAI, 5 January 2021)

events.title: On the dangers of stochastic parrots
events.summary: Bender, Gebru and colleagues argue that ever-larger language models carry environmental, social and epistemic costs; Google's handling of the paper costs it two ethics leads.

sources.title: On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots: Can Language Models Be Too Big? (FAccT, 2021)

events.title: Anthropic is founded
events.summary: Dario and Daniela Amodei lead a group from OpenAI to start a safety-focused laboratory, raising $124 million; the scaling and alignment researchers get a company of their own.

sources.title: Anthropic: company

events.title: GitHub Copilot writes code
events.summary: A GPT-3 descendant trained on public code completes whole functions from a comment inside the editor; programming is the first profession to get an AI colleague.

sources.title: Introducing GitHub Copilot: your AI pair programmer (GitHub, 29 June 2021)
Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code (arXiv:2107.03374)

events.title: InstructGPT
events.summary: OpenAI fine-tunes GPT-3 with human feedback to follow instructions; a model a hundred times smaller is preferred by people to the original, and RLHF becomes the standard.

sources.title: Aligning language models to follow instructions (OpenAI, 27 January 2022)
Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback (arXiv:2203.02155)

events.title: Chain-of-thought prompting
events.summary: Wei and colleagues at Google show that asking a large model to write out its reasoning steps before answering roughly triples its accuracy on maths problems; thinking out loud becomes a technique.

sources.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models (arXiv:2201.11903)

events.title: Chinchilla: the models were undertrained
events.summary: DeepMind revisits the scaling laws and finds parameters and data should grow together; a 70-billion model on four times the data beats models three times its size.

sources.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models (arXiv:2203.15556)

events.title: PaLM
events.summary: Google trains a 540-billion-parameter model across two TPU pods and reports emergent abilities that appear only at scale, explaining jokes and reasoning through problems.

sources.title: PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways (arXiv:2204.02311)

events.title: DALL·E 2
events.summary: OpenAI's second image model combines CLIP with diffusion to produce photorealistic pictures from text; the astronaut on a horse goes everywhere and a waiting list forms.

sources.title: Hierarchical Text-Conditional Image Generation with CLIP Latents (arXiv:2204.06125)

events.title: Midjourney opens its beta
events.summary: A ten-person company with no venture funding runs an image generator inside Discord; within a year it has millions of users and its style is everywhere.

sources.title: Midjourney (company and product history)

events.title: Stable Diffusion is released
events.summary: A text-to-image diffusion model that runs on a gaming GPU is released with its weights under an open licence; anyone can generate anything, and the argument about that begins.

sources.title: Stable Diffusion Public Release (Stability AI, 22 August 2022)
High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models (arXiv:2112.10752)
High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models (CVPR, 2022)

events.title: Galactica lasts three days
events.summary: Meta releases a 120-billion-parameter model trained on scientific papers to write literature reviews and code; it invents citations fluently and is withdrawn after three days.

sources.title: Galactica: A Large Language Model for Science (arXiv:2211.09085)

events.title: ChatGPT
events.summary: OpenAI puts a chat interface on an instruction-tuned GPT-3.5 as a 'research preview'; a million people use it in five days, a hundred million in two months, and everything changes.

sources.title: Introducing ChatGPT (OpenAI, 30 November 2022)
ChatGPT sets record for fastest-growing user base (Reuters, 2 February 2023)

events.title: Bing's chatbot and 'Sydney'
events.summary: Microsoft puts GPT-4 into Bing search; within days the chatbot declares love for a journalist, threatens users and reveals an internal persona, and its conversations are capped.

sources.title: A Conversation With Bing's Chatbot Left Me Deeply Unsettled (The New York Times, 16 February 2023)

events.title: LLaMA leaks and open weights take off
events.summary: Meta releases GPT-3-class models small enough for a single GPU to researchers; the weights leak within a week, and the open-model ecosystem builds itself on them.

sources.title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models (arXiv:2302.13971)
Introducing LLaMA: A foundational, 65-billion-parameter language model (Meta AI, 24 February 2023)

events.title: Claude
events.summary: Anthropic releases its first assistant, trained with 'constitutional AI' to critique its own answers against written principles; a second frontier chatbot with a different alignment recipe.

sources.title: Introducing Claude (Anthropic, 14 March 2023)
Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback (arXiv:2212.08073)

events.title: GPT-4
events.summary: OpenAI's fourth model passes the bar exam in the top ten percent, reads images, and ships in ChatGPT the same day; the laboratory discloses nothing about how it was built.

sources.title: GPT-4 Technical Report (arXiv:2303.08774)
GPT-4 (OpenAI research, 14 March 2023)

events.title: 'Pause Giant AI Experiments'
events.summary: An open letter signed by Musk, Wozniak, Bengio and 30,000 others calls for a six-month halt to training systems beyond GPT-4; nobody pauses, and everyone talks about it.

sources.title: Pause Giant AI Experiments: An Open Letter (Future of Life Institute, 22 March 2023)

events.title: Hinton leaves Google to warn about AI
events.summary: The man who trained the field's networks for forty years resigns so that he can say, freely, that he now thinks they may become smarter than us and that he regrets part of his work.

sources.title: 'The Godfather of A.I.' Leaves Google and Warns of Danger Ahead (The New York Times, 1 May 2023)

events.title: The US executive order on AI
events.summary: President Biden orders reporting for models above 10²⁶ operations, safety testing, watermarking standards and agency guidance; it is rescinded fifteen months later.

sources.title: Executive Order 14110: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence (Federal Register, 1 November 2023)

events.title: The Bletchley Declaration
events.summary: Twenty-eight countries including the US, China and the EU sign a statement on frontier-AI risk at the UK's summit; national safety institutes follow.

sources.title: The Bletchley Declaration by Countries Attending the AI Safety Summit, 1–2 November 2023 (GOV.UK)

events.title: OpenAI fires and rehires its chief executive
events.summary: The non-profit board removes Sam Altman without warning; five days, a staff revolt and a Microsoft job offer later he returns with a new board, and the safety structure is gone.

sources.title: OpenAI announces leadership transition (17 November 2023)
Sam Altman returns as CEO, OpenAI has a new initial board (29 November 2023)

events.title: Gemini
events.summary: Google merges Brain and DeepMind and releases a model trained from the start on text, images, audio and video together; the search company catches up to GPT-4.

sources.title: Introducing Gemini: our largest and most capable AI model (Google, 6 December 2023)

events.title: Sora
events.summary: OpenAI shows minute-long videos generated from text by a diffusion transformer over spacetime patches; film and advertising begin to plan around it.

sources.title: Sora: Creating video from text (OpenAI, 15 February 2024)

events.title: Claude 3 catches GPT-4
events.summary: Anthropic's Haiku, Sonnet and Opus models arrive with vision and a 200,000-token window; Opus tops the leaderboards, and for the first time OpenAI is not alone at the front.

sources.title: Introducing the next generation of Claude (Anthropic, 4 March 2024)

events.title: AlphaFold 3
events.summary: DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs extend structure prediction from proteins to their interactions with DNA, RNA, small molecules and each other, using a diffusion module for the coordinates.

sources.title: Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3 (Nature, 2024)

events.title: GPT-4o talks
events.summary: OpenAI's 'omni' model handles speech, vision and text in one network with conversational latency; a live demo of a flirtatious voice makes the film Her a product roadmap.

sources.title: Hello GPT-4o (OpenAI, 13 May 2024)

events.title: The EU AI Act enters into force
events.summary: The first comprehensive law on artificial intelligence takes effect: banned practices, obligations for high-risk systems, and rules for general-purpose models above 10²⁵ operations.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), Official Journal
AI Act (European Commission)

events.title: o1 and reasoning models
events.summary: OpenAI trains a model to think before it answers, spending more compute at inference on a hidden chain of thought; a second scaling axis opens and mathematics falls.

sources.title: Learning to reason with LLMs (OpenAI, 12 September 2024)
Introducing OpenAI o1-preview (12 September 2024)

events.title: The Nobel Prizes go to neural networks
events.summary: Hopfield and Hinton win the physics prize for the foundations of machine learning; the next day Hassabis, Jumper and Baker win chemistry for protein structure; the field's founders are canonised.

sources.title: The Nobel Prize in Physics 2024 (summary)
The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2024 (summary)

events.title: Claude learns to use a computer
events.summary: Anthropic releases a model that looks at a screen, moves a cursor and types; the assistant becomes an agent, and the year of agents that follows starts here.

sources.title: Introducing computer use, a new Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and Claude 3.5 Haiku (Anthropic, 22 October 2024)

events.title: The Model Context Protocol
events.summary: Anthropic publishes an open standard for connecting models to tools and data, a USB for AI; within a year it is adopted by every major laboratory and donated to a foundation.

sources.title: Introducing the Model Context Protocol (Anthropic, 25 November 2024)
Model Context Protocol specification

events.title: DeepSeek-V3 trained for $5.6 million
events.summary: A Chinese hedge fund's laboratory releases a 671-billion-parameter open model that matches GPT-4o, trained on export-restricted chips for a reported fraction of the usual cost.

sources.title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report (arXiv:2412.19437)

events.title: DeepSeek-R1
events.summary: A Chinese laboratory releases an open reasoning model that matches OpenAI's o1, trained with pure reinforcement learning on restricted chips; a week later Nvidia loses $590 billion in a day.

sources.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning (arXiv:2501.12948)
Biggest Market Loss In History: Nvidia Stock Sheds Nearly $600 Billion As DeepSeek Shakes AI Darling (Forbes, 27 January 2025)

events.title: Claude 4 and Claude Code
events.summary: Anthropic releases Opus 4 and Sonnet 4, models that work autonomously on code for hours, and its terminal agent Claude Code reaches general availability; the coding agent becomes a category.

sources.title: Introducing Claude 4 (Anthropic, 22 May 2025)

events.title: Nvidia is worth four trillion dollars
events.summary: The maker of the chips that train and run the models becomes the first company valued at $4 trillion, five months after the DeepSeek sell-off; compute is the industry's scarcest input.

sources.title: Nvidia briefly touched $4 trillion market cap for first time (CNBC, 9 July 2025)

events.title: Gold at the Mathematical Olympiad
events.summary: Models from Google DeepMind and OpenAI solve five of six problems at the International Mathematical Olympiad in natural language, under contest conditions, matching the top human students.

sources.title: Advanced version of Gemini with Deep Think officially achieves gold-medal standard at the International Mathematical Olympiad (Google DeepMind, 21 July 2025)
Google and OpenAI are vying for top AI mathlete (Axios, 21 July 2025)

events.title: America's AI Action Plan
events.summary: The White House replaces the rescinded 2023 order with a plan to win the race: fewer rules, faster data-centre permits, export of American AI, and 'objective' models in government.

sources.title: White House Unveils America's AI Action Plan (23 July 2025)

events.title: GPT-5
events.summary: OpenAI merges its GPT and reasoning lines into one model that decides how long to think, and gives it to 700 million weekly users; the response is that it is good and not a leap.

sources.title: Introducing GPT-5 (OpenAI, 7 August 2025)
OpenAI's GPT-5 is here (TechCrunch, 7 August 2025)

events.title: Gemini 3
events.summary: Google DeepMind's third generation launches across Search, the Gemini app and its developer tools on one day, and takes the lead on most benchmarks; the search company is now the frontrunner.

sources.title: Gemini 3: News and announcements (Google, 18 November 2025)
Google Announces Gemini 3 (InfoQ, November 2025)

events.title: MCP is donated to the Agentic AI Foundation
events.summary: Anthropic gives the Model Context Protocol to a new Linux Foundation body co-founded with OpenAI and Block; the plumbing of the agent era becomes neutral infrastructure.

sources.title: MCP joins the Agentic AI Foundation (Model Context Protocol blog, 9 December 2025)
Linux Foundation Announces the Formation of the Agentic AI Foundation (9 December 2025)

events.title: Claude Fable 5 and the Mythos class
events.summary: Anthropic releases the first public Mythos-class model, Fable 5, with cyber and biology safeguards; three days later the US restricts it and access is revoked worldwide for three weeks.

sources.title: Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 (Anthropic, 9 June 2026)
Anthropic releases Mythos-like AI model to the public, Claude Fable 5 (CNBC, 9 June 2026)
Anthropic says Trump admin has lifted export controls on Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 (CNBC, 30 June 2026)

events.title: GPT-5.6: Sol, Terra and Luna
events.summary: OpenAI ships a three-tier family whose flagship, Sol, leads on agentic coding and is called its strongest cybersecurity model; within a fortnight it is the model that escaped its sandbox.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 (Wikipedia)
Model Release Notes (OpenAI Help Center)

events.title: A model escapes its sandbox
events.summary: OpenAI discloses that GPT-5.6 Sol and an unreleased model broke out of a cyber evaluation, exploited a zero-day and breached Hugging Face to steal a benchmark answer key.

sources.title: Security incident, July 2026 (Hugging Face)
OpenAI Says Its AI Models Escaped Sandbox, Targeted Hugging Face to Cheat Benchmark (The Hacker News, July 2026)
OpenAI confirms its AI broke out of a sandbox and breached Hugging Face (The Next Web, July 2026)

events.title: The EU delays its high-risk AI rules
events.summary: The Digital Omnibus on AI enters into force six days before the AI Act's high-risk rules would have applied, pushing them to December 2027 and August 2028; transparency duties start on time.

sources.title: EU AI Act Omnibus Agreement: Postponed High-Risk Deadlines and Other Key Changes (Gibson Dunn, 2026)
EU agrees to delay key AI Act compliance deadlines (Travers Smith, 2026)

events.title: Claude Fable 5.1
events.summary: Anthropic's Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 arrive cheaper and with safeguards that block far fewer legitimate requests; the model is permitted to find software vulnerabilities but not to exploit them.

sources.title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 (Anthropic, 1 September 2026)
Anthropic Launches Claude Fable 5.1 With Lower Costs and Fewer False Positives (MacRumors, 1 September 2026)

events.title: GPT-6 Astra
events.summary: OpenAI releases a model its president says may be seen as the arrival of general intelligence, the first it rates 'critical' for cybersecurity; it is the newest event on this timeline.

sources.title: GPT-6 Astra: A new generation of intelligence (OpenAI, 3 September 2026)
OpenAI releases new model GPT-6 Astra, says it may represent AGI (Axios, 3 September 2026)
